---
title: "Statistical Architecture Framework"
---

SAF is a shared way for national statistical offices to describe how they turn data into official statistics — and to change how they do it without breaking things.

It is aimed at everyone involved in that work: methodologists, statisticians, data and IT staff, quality and privacy officers, managers and CIOs... **No architecture background is assumed**, on this site or in the framework itself.

::: {.callout-tip title="Where to start"}
If you have ten minutes, read **SAF in Brief**. If you want to try SAF on one of your own statistical products, read **Getting Started** and do the exercise at the end. The **Framework** is the reference you dip into afterwards.
:::

## The one idea worth knowing first

SAF splits statistical production into stages that hand data to each other at defined points called **steady states**. At each handover the data is finished to a known quality, given a version and an identifier, and passed on with a description of what was done to it. Nothing else about the next stage's inner workings needs to be known.

That single arrangement is what lets an office modernise one part of its production — a collection channel, an editing engine, a publication platform — without disturbing the rest, and lets it show exactly how any published figure was produced.

The formal model behind all of this is available in archimate format ([to complete](link))
